identity.name: Portugieser Chronograph

case.bezel: no bezel — fixed silver-plated dial with a railway-track minute scale

identity.one_liner: IWC's flagship round chronograph, pairing the oversized Portugieser case with two sub-dials and a railway-track minute scale borrowed from marine chronometer dials.

narrative.story: The Portugieser line began in 1939 with reference 325, a 41.5mm wristwatch built around IWC's flat pocket-watch Caliber 74 rather than a movement designed for a normal-size wrist case — which is why the family still runs oversized relative to IWC's other collections. The modern Portugieser Chronograph carries that oversized-case identity forward with a two-register chronograph layout and a dial minute track styled after marine chronometers, IWC's original nineteenth-century business before it became known for wristwatches.
narrative.collector_notes: IWC also produces an in-house-movement Portugieser Chronograph generation (caliber 69355) alongside this cal. 79350-based reference; the two look similar at a glance but differ in movement architecture, so confirm the caliber via the case back or reference number before assuming which generation a listing describes.
